newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NEC expects China sales to grow 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: NEC expects China sales to grow 25 percent.

text.p: A senior NEC Corp official said on Thursday that the company expects China sales to grow 25 percent to around 140 billion yen in the year ending March 31, 1998.
Iwao Shinohara, NEC associate senior vice president, also told Reuters that NEC aims to boost sales in China to US$2.2 billion by 2000.
"We expect our place in China to grow sharply this year to around 140 billion yen, or slightly less than 150 billion yen," Shinohara said.

He said about 70 percent sales growth will come from telecommunications equipment such as exchange systems, and the rest will come from computer chips, personal computers and household electric appliances.
He added, however, that sales of chips and computers will grow at a faster rate than sales of telecom equipment due to a changing market structure.

Shinohara also said Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp's entry into the international market this year will be a big advantage for NEC and other Japanese telecom equipment makers in their Asia business.

"We Japanese makers have been behind European and American rivals in Asia markets, particularly in China because big Japanese carriers were not allowed to provide operations in overseas markets," he said.
Under NEC's medium-term business plan, NEC set a sales target in China of $2.2 billion for 2000, Shinohara said.
